fish-and-vegetables-including-carrots-br.title: Fish with Vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy)

content.title: About
content.content: The dish combines tender fish (such as cod, salmon or hake) with fresh vegetables: carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale, Swiss chard). It is prepared without potatoes and without tomato‑based sauce, making it light and nutrient‑dense.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fish is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, which support heart and brain health.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for its anti‑cancer properties.
Dark‑green leafy greens are high in vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A for vision.
The combination of fish and vegetables provides a complete set of essential amino acids and micronutrients.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Omega‑3s from fish lower triglycerides and inflammation, while potassium from vegetables helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: Vitamin C from broccoli and beta‑carotene from carrots enhance the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Vision protection
items.content: Beta‑carotene and lutein from carrots and broccoli protect the retina from oxidative stress.

items.title: Reduced risk of chronic disease
items.content: Antioxidants and phytochemicals in the vegetables together with omega‑3s lower the risk of diabetes and certain cancers.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species can contain mercury or cadmium; choosing smaller species and limiting frequency reduces exposure.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions of broccoli may cause gas in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fish can be baked, poached, or steamed, while vegetables are best lightly sautéed or steamed to retain crunch and nutrients. Combine them on a plate, drizzle with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh fish in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for up to 2 days, and store vegetables in the crisper drawer at 4‑6 °C for up to 5 days. For freezing, pack fish in airtight bags and blanch vegetables before freezing; they keep well for up to 3 months.

infant-formula-enfamil-infant-powder-mad.title: Enfamil Infant, powder, prepared with tap water

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Infant is a powdered infant formula designed for babies from birth to 12 months. It provides proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals essential for growth and development. Preparation is done with clean tap water according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enfamil is one of the most recognized infant nutrition brands, produced by Mead Johnson.
The formula is enriched with DHA and ARA – fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
It is formulated according to WHO recommendations for early childhood nutrition.
The product has undergone clinical trials confirming its safety and efficacy.
Enfamil Infant is available in various package sizes for parental convenience.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: The blend offers an optimal balance of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, B‑vitamins, vitamin D, and calcium to promote healthy bone and muscle growth.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA help build neural pathways, enhancing cognitive function and vision in infants.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C, zinc, and iron strengthen the immune system, increasing resistance to infections.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Proteins are partially hydrolyzed, making them easier to digest and reducing the risk of colic.

items.title: Balanced blood‑sugar level
items.content: Carbohydrates are provided as lactose, which raises blood glucose slowly, delivering steady energy.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergy to casein or whey; if symptoms appear, discontinue use and consult a pediatrician.

items.title: Incorrect reconstitution
items.content: Too concentrated or too diluted formula can cause dehydration or over‑feeding; always follow the water‑to‑powder ratio.

items.title: Water temperature control
items.content: Water should be warm (~37 °C); water that is too hot can degrade nutrients, while cold water may cause discomfort.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: After opening, use the formula within 30 days and store it in a dry, light‑protected place.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Measure the recommended amount of powder (usually 1 scoop per 30 ml of water), add clean warm tap water, and stir thoroughly until fully dissolved. Allow the mixture to cool to body temperature before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, seal tightly and use within one month.

content.title: About
content.content: Mixed nuts, unroasted (2270) is a blend of various nuts such as almonds, hazelnuts, cashews, walnuts, peanuts and others, combined in balanced proportions. The nuts are not heat‑treated, preserving their natural flavor, aroma and the maximum amount of nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mixed nuts are often used in cooking to add texture and flavor to dishes.
Unroasted nuts retain more vitamins and antioxidants compared with roasted ones.
The blend typically contains about 50 % healthy fats by weight.
Some mixes include dried fruit or seeds, increasing their nutritional value.
Mixed nuts are usually sold in airtight packaging to prevent oil oxidation.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: The blend provides monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Nuts supply quality protein that aids tissue repair and helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Contains vitamin E and B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant, while B‑vitamins participate in energy metabolism.

items.title: Packed with minerals
items.content: Magnesium, phosphorus, zinc and copper in the mix are essential for bones, nervous system and immunity.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The dietary fiber in nuts promotes healthy bowel function and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions, ranging from mild symptoms to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Nuts are energy‑dense, so portion size should be monitored, especially on calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Whole nuts can pose a choking risk for young children; finely chopped or ground nuts are safer.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Certain nuts (e.g., almonds) contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mixed nuts can be enjoyed as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or used in sauces. Soaking the nuts for a few hours can improve digestibility and soften the skins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid or have off‑flavors.

content.title: About
content.content: Soup, cream of vegetable (4867) is a ready‑to‑eat vegetable cream soup made from selected vegetables, cream, and aromatic spices. It has a smooth texture, mild creamy flavor, and is suitable as a light starter or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetable cream soup is often used in diet nutrition because of its low calorie content and high vitamin levels.
The blend typically includes carrot, pumpkin, broccoli, and cauliflower, providing a wide range of nutrients.
The creamy base softens the taste and helps absorb fat‑soluble vitamins more effectively.
The product can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days after opening.
Some versions add herbs such as basil and parsley to enhance aroma.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The vegetables provide vitamins B6 and B9, which support metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety, and supports gut health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The creamy component contains a modest amount of healthy fats, making the soup suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Beta‑carotene and vitamin C from the vegetables help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and other micronutrients contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cream component may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Some varieties contain added salt; individuals monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Preservative content
items.content: Ready‑made soups may contain preservatives; those sensitive should choose a product without additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the vegetable cream soup over low heat, stirring, until it reaches 70‑80 °C. It can be served on its own, or enriched with cooked chicken pieces, seafood, or fresh herbs for variety.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. After opening, consume within 5 days. Freezing may alter texture, so refrigeration is recommended.

content.title: About
content.content: Tamarind is the fruit of the tropical tree Tamarindus indica, native to Africa, Asia and South America. The pods have a sweet‑sour flavor, reminiscent of lemon, dates and caramel. Inside is a soft pulp surrounded by a dark brown shell and large seeds.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tamarind has been used in cooking for over 4,000 years and is mentioned in ancient Egyptian texts.
Tamarind paste and juice are key ingredients in Thai, Indian and Mexican cuisines.
The tamarind tree can reach 25 m in height and live more than 200 years.
Tamarind seeds are rich in iron and are used in traditional medicine to treat anemia.
In some cultures tamarind is a symbol of hospitality and is served with tea.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Tamarind provides a notable amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: High levels of soluble and insoluble fiber promote digestive health and help regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium in tamarind supports normal heart function and fluid‑electrolyte balance.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Phenolics and carotenoids in tamarind help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports liver function
items.content: Traditionally tamarind is used to aid liver health and detoxification.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergy to tamarind, resulting in skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Because of its high acidity, large amounts can irritate the stomach and cause heartburn.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened tamarind paste contains added sugars, which should be considered by people with diabetes.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Tamarind may enhance the effects of certain medications, such as anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tamarind is used fresh, as a paste, concentrated juice, or dried pods. It is added to sauces, marinades, soups, curries, drinks and desserts. Pods can be soaked in water to soften the pulp, then the juice is squeezed out.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried pods or paste in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. In the refrigerator the product lasts up to 6 months. Discard if mold, off‑odor or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Vegetarian Stroganoff is a plant‑based adaptation of the classic Russian beef stroganoff. Instead of beef, mushrooms (commonly button or oyster) and soy‑based proteins are used, while the sauce is made from plant butter, onion, sour cream or coconut cream, and tomato paste. The dish retains a rich, creamy flavor and aroma while being suitable for vegetarians and those reducing meat consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original beef stroganoff originated in Russia in the 19th century and was made with beef, sour cream, and onions.
The vegetarian version gained popularity in the 1970s as demand for plant‑based alternatives grew.
Mushrooms mimic the texture of meat and their natural umami boosts the sauce’s depth.
Some recipes replace mushrooms with dried tofu to add extra protein.
It is commonly served over pasta, rice, or mashed potatoes, making it a versatile main.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Mushrooms and soy proteins provide essential amino acids needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using plant butter and cream alternatives reduces saturated fat compared with the traditional recipe.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Mushrooms contain riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The vegetables and mushrooms add fiber that aids healthy digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomato paste and cream (or coconut cream) supply lycopene and vitamin E, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to certain mushroom varieties.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared tomato paste or soy sauce can raise sodium levels; choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Plant butter and cream make the dish calorie‑rich; portion control is advised for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Certain mushrooms contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot over pasta (e.g., tagliatelle), rice, couscous, or mashed potatoes. Garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill. A squeeze of lemon juice can brighten the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of plant milk or water to restore creaminess. Freezing is not recommended as the sauce may separate.
